newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 1.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- A wave of speculation on the Irish pound yesterday saw it lose almost three percent of its value in just one day.

- Ireland's Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn on Wednesday moved to curb the slide in the Irish pound, saying Ireland would not necessarily join a single currency at its official central rate in the European currency grid.

- The ISEQ index of share prices in Dublin surged by over 53 points to a new record level on Wednesday as investors responded to continued strength on Wall Street and opportunities created by the weakening Irish pound.
- The Irish government's new sex education programme has received a major setback following its rejection by most of the teaching staff at a primary school.
- Britain's Labour Party goes into today's general election with a huge opinion poll lead and poised to take power after 18 years in opposition.
- Irish financial markets are facing into a period of uncertainty after a sharp drop in the value of the Irish pound because of heavy selling by international investors.
- About 1,400 new jobs in the Shannon region in County Clare have been announced.
- The fate of the 136 million Irish pounds bid by workers in Ireland's Telecom Eireann company hangs in the balance.
- A survey shows Irish people are becoming more careless about exposure to the sun.
- Talks to resolve the protest over new security arrangements by loyalist prisoners at the Maze Prison in Northern Ireland continued on Wednesday.
- Speculators have made over 40 million Irish pounds in the past week in an attack on the punt that looks set to push up bank and mortgage interest rates within days.
- A 10-year battle to attract a major overseas industry to Ennis, County Clare, paid off on Wednesday when Ireland's Employment Minister Richard Bruton announced a 600-job plant for the town.
